claims.text: EAM references used in standard TOR-TILD inadequately represent the many atomic configurations of high-temperature HEA liquids.
High-temperature multicomponent HEAs exhibit highly disordered atomic configurations in their solid and liquid states near melting.
The EAM reference should be replaced by an ML interatomic potential trained on a diverse set of ab initio liquid configurations.
A neural-network potential or Gaussian approximation potential could serve as the proposed ML reference.
Training on high-temperature ab initio liquid configurations enables the ML potential to reproduce the complex configurational spectrum of the ab initio liquid.
The trained ML potential captures a broader and more accurate range of atomic environments than an EAM model.
More accurate representation of liquid atomic environments improves reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap produces a smoother and shorter thermodynamic-integration path.
Using the ML reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path-mismatch error relative to TOR-TILD using an EAM reference.
The thermodynamic-integration path-mismatch error is predicted to decrease by 30–50% relative to traditional EAM-based TOR-TILD.
The intervention is applicable to typical multicomponent HEA compositions.
The intervention is applicable near and slightly above the alloys' melting temperatures.
Performance may be limited for configurations exhibiting disorder beyond the ML training domain or under nonequilibrium conditions.
The relative performance of the ML and EAM references can be tested under identical temperature conditions using ab initio free-energy benchmarks.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement in phase-space overlap and at least a 30% reduction in path-mismatch error would falsify the hypothesis.
